angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 292,194 km at 44.72 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.3633 +/- 0.0179 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 44.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.42 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5489 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract): 292,194 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.41 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5489 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3547 +/- 157 K from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5489 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gomez Barrientos et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5489 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5489.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.804, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, UCAC4 508-048355: main object type Em*, Emission-line Star
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5489 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.60776, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
